K2.basis: Unchanged data since round 1. Re-run on the round-2 bytes: gate to server, gate to containment and broker to maintenance each fail exactly A59.planeon_server_t, A59.planeon_contain_t and A59.planeon_maint_t. Round 1's exhaustive probe (124 out-of-procAccess pairs to the eight targets, all caught) applies, because matrix.json is byte-identical.

K3.basis: A66 fails for init_t load_policy before the seal (re-run). M54 and M55 reproduce. A23 pins setenforce. The README's claim is now scoped to the modelled states (F3).

K4.basis: The evaluator comment is corrected (F1). The dir create statement now includes the create_sid branch under SBLABEL_MNT (F4). The kernfs xattr, SE_SBGENFS and cgroup_seclabel/SBLABEL_MNT statements match v6.12 hooks.c. S11 targets planeon_cgroup_slice_t, the parent-computed object when no fscreate context is set.

K6.basis: The round-2 brief keeps 109 assertions, which equals the matrix.

F1.basis: The GENFS_CATEGORIES comment now says kernfs (cgroup2) supports security xattrs, that no planeon cgroup node carries one, and that labels therefore come from the path rules. This is accurate for v6.12 (SE_SBGENFS_XATTR for cgroup2; bpffs gets SE_SBGENFS only). The diff against round1/scripts/selinux_matrix_v2.py touches only those comment lines.

F2.basis: The introduction states K1 (W02a-F, T04, W01's record; pinned-policy scope, boolean preservation, early window, boot-entry discriminator or explicit statement) and K5 (DelegateSubgroup=broker, the maintenance unit writing booleans in init_t, portcon of planeon_server_port_t). Both match v3 status.json carriedFindings. Two older K1 mentions still list only W02a-F and T04 (G1, NOTE).

F3.basis: The K3 row now claims only that no load_policy grant is reachable in the two modelled enrolled states. It states that the single-policy property rests on decision 10 and on the digest and booleans W01's record pins, the K1 dependency, and names the unmodelled combination systemd can reach.

F4.basis: The fscreate text matches v6.12 selinux_determine_inode_label: create_sid is used when SBLABEL_MNT is set, and for cgroup2 that holds when cgroup_seclabel is enabled (selinux_is_genfs_special_handling). The W03/T04 requirement that no creator of a planeon cgroup sets an fscreate context is added. The reason for listing cgroup_seclabel is stated. Its premise that base policies declare it holds for the two upstreams I read: refpolicy main and Fedora selinux-policy rawhide both have 'policycap cgroup_seclabel;' in policy/policy_capabilities.

F5.basis: The per-target scope is stated in the K2 row and the A59.* row: the five resident roles, the writer, containment and the maintenance domain, not the admin login. Re-run: gate to admin passes all 109 assertions, as disclosed. One precision note, not a finding: the README calls the admin login's /proc 'host policy', yet allowed() closes it (False, not None), because procAccess grants no reader. The matrix denies it without asserting it.

modelExecution: One process at a time, each under 60 s, with 'uv run --offline --frozen --no-sync python' and UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT set to the harness-onion .venv. p1_replay.py (3.7 s) imported the round-2 scripts/selinux_matrix_v2.py and checked: check_matrix, failed_assertions (109, none failed), w02a_slots, all 1,873 access checks and all 55 mutation checks (zero mismatches). It then ran in-memory probes: the three round-3 /proc pairs, init_t load_policy before the seal, and gate to admin /proc. Two curl fetches (25 s cap each) retrieved the upstream policy_capabilities files. Work paused on the coordinator's PAUSE and resumed only after RESUME. No repository file was written.
